summary: Adds an admin route that deletes one user by id and a purge route that deletes a list of users.

findings.title: Delete user route lacks admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route omits the requireAdmin middleware that its sibling routes use. The handler deletes the user named in the URL without any authorization check.
findings.consequence: Any caller who can reach the server can delete any user account. The caller only needs to guess or enumerate user ids.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route, as the GET /users and POST /users/purge routes do.

findings.title: Purge deletions float outside the request
findings.problem: The forEach callback starts async removeUser calls, and nothing awaits them. db.removeUser throws for an unknown id, so each failure becomes an unhandled rejection.
findings.consequence: One unknown id in the purge list crashes the Node process on current Node versions. The handler also reports every id as removed before any deletion finishes.
findings.fix: Await all deletions with Promise.allSettled, then report how many succeeded.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete routes have no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds two delete routes, and the repository contains no tests for them.
findings.consequence: Nothing will catch a regression in the auth check or in purge error handling.
findings.fix: Add tests for the single delete and purge routes, covering auth and an unknown id.
